chunks: O those whose bodies are present,
whose wits are absent, whose desires are scattered, whose rulers are on trial,
Your leader obeys Allāh but you disobey him,
while the leader of the people of Syria disobeys Allāh but they obey him.
By Allāh, I wish Mu‘āwiyah exchanges with me like Dinars with Dirhams, so that he takes from me ten of you and gives me one from them!

key_terms.صَرْفَ الدِّينَارِ بِالدِّرْهَمِ: exchange of dinars for dirhams (metaphor for unequal exchange)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali mean by wishing to exchange his followers with Mu'awiya's?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) critiques the spiritual dissonance of his companions, whose bodies were present but minds absent, contrasting their selective obedience with the blind compliance of the Syrians under Mu'awiya. This famous metaphor of exchanging 'ten of you for one of them' underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) and conscious devotion over mere political utility or passive submission. The passage reflects the early Umayyad period's shifting dynamics, where loyalty was often measured by political alignment rather than religious fidelity.

en.sayed-ali-raza: O those whose bodies are present but wits are absent, and whose wishes are scattered.
Your leader obeys Allāh but you disobeyed him while the leader of the people of Syria (ash-Shām) disobeys Allāh but they obey him.
By Allāh, I wish Mu‘āwiyah exchanges with me like Dinars with Dirhams, so that he takes from me ten of you and give me one from them.
